title: Guaranteed audit delivery with sequenced replay and policy-led routing
creator: Ethan Zhang
description:
Problem: Customers integrating Redwood audit events into external SIEMs (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, generic webhooks) report intermittent duplicates, reordering, and long tail delivery spikes during load spikes or transient downstream backpressure. Current forwarder retries aggressively but lacks per-tenant sequencing for ordered analysis in SIEMs, and there is no formal policy routing to respect customer SLAs (e.g., gold customers prefer lower-latency best-effort, enterprise customers require stronger delivery guarantees).

Goal: Implement a hybrid-buffered audit forwarder that provides configurable delivery guarantees per-route (at-least-once with dedup, or ordered-append with best-effort replay), deterministic sequenced replay for tenant-aware ordering, and policy-led routing that selects delivery strategy based on route-level SLOs. The system should integrate with Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and generic webhook sinks, support mTLS/HMAC authentication, and expose observability for delivery latency, retry storms, and duplication rates.

Key design choices: hybrid buffering (in-memory LRU + persistent write-ahead LSM), sequence aliasing to allow logical ordering without global monotonic counters, ack windows with compact checkpoints to limit persisted state, and pluggable adapter contracts for external sinks to provide backpressure signals (HTTP 429/503 + Retry-After, or custom X-Redwood-Ack). We choose at-least-once by default with idempotency tokens and optional exactly-once-ish semantics for enterprise routes using external dedup stores and consumer-side sequence checks.

Out of scope: fully transactional exactly-once across all sinks, multi-region cross-tenant deduplicated ordering (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Audit forwarder supports route-level delivery policies: best-effort, at-least-once-with-dedup, ordered-with-replay
Splunk HEC and Datadog adapters implement ack-window protocol and surface backpressure reasons in logs
Sequence aliasing guarantees per-tenant ordering for ordered routes within a configurable replay window (default 48h)
End-to-end tests show <=1% duplicate rate for at-least-once-with-dedup under chaos scenarios and no reordering for ordered routes in integration tests
Metrics exposed: delivery_latency_p50/p95/p99, retry_rate, duplicate_rate, persist_queue_size, ack_window_lag
Security: all sink connections support mTLS and HMAC signing; keys rotate without downtime
SLOs defined and validated in staging: 99.9% deliveries within 60s for enterprise routes under normal load
tasks: Design: finalize sequence alias format and checkpoint compacting algorithm
Implement: hybrid buffer (mem + WAL LSM) with per-tenant namespaces
Adapter: add ack-window and backpressure handling to Splunk HEC adapter
Adapter: implement Datadog Logs adapter with idempotency headers
Integration tests: write chaos tests (downstream 503/slow, reboots, disk full)
Observability: add Grafana dashboards and tracing spans for delivery pipeline
Security: run internal security review and add KMS rotation test
Docs: update Console docs for route-level delivery policy UI and runbook
comments: 2026-02-18 - Ethan Zhang: Created ticket after design sync. Initial proposal attached to Confluence (see link). Recommended default policy = at-least-once-with-dedup for hosted routes.
2026-02-24 - Marisol Ortega: Design review notes - prefer sequence aliasing over global counters to avoid cross-tenant coordination. Added requirement for compact checkpoints to keep storage small.
2026-02-28 - Review (Security): Alice Monroe - verify HMAC header format and key rotation semantics. Flagged requirement to support mTLS to satisfy enterprise compliance.

2026-03-03 - Engineering update: PoC hybrid buffer implemented (mem + WAL) and basic Splunk adapter wired up (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-forwarder/pull/312). Observed sustained throughput of 4k req/s on dev cluster with low p99 latency.
2026-03-05 - QA: Added chaos test that simulates Splunk HEC 503 with Retry-After header. Current behavior: retries back off, WAL grows; need to add compaction TTL to avoid storage blowup.

2026-03-07 - Product feedback (Priya Shah): Need UI knobs in Console to select policy per-route and to escalate retries for enterprise SLA. Also request ability to opt-in to exactly-once-ish dedup using external Redis store.

2026-03-08 - Marisol Ortega: Implemented ack-window checkpointing and compacted checkpoint format (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-forwarder/pull/339). Added unit tests for sequence alias wrap-around. Planning integration tests next week.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable new forwarder for internal tenant only. Validate metrics and disk usage for 72h.
Phase 2 (canary): opt-in 5 customers (mix of gold and enterprise) with Console UI flag. Monitor duplicate_rate and p99 latency.
Phase 3 (gradual): enable per-route default policy switch for all hosted routes; keep legacy forwarder as fallback for 14 days
Phase 4 (GA): deprecate legacy config after 30 days of healthy metrics and sign-off from Security/ProdEng
test_plan: Unit tests for sequence aliasing (wrap-around, tenant namespace isolation)
Integration tests: Splunk HEC adapter under 503/429/slow downstream
End-to-end QA: compare events received in Splunk index with original stream to calculate duplicate and reorder rates
Load test: sustained 10k/s ingestion with mixed route policies to validate WAL compaction and throughput
Security test: verify mTLS handshake and HMAC validation with rotated keys
